questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been in Italy for some months before and had learned Italian. I chose Rome because I wanted to try living in such a big city. I also chose it because the university LUISS is academically good according to international rankings.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Compared to other Italian university, Luiss provided a lot of information. The student orientation service was also quite effective and quick to respond. Besides this, there is a big volunteer organisation of local students welcoming the exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance both from the student mobility service and the Erasmus organisation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of information was available very close to semesterstart or only after the semester started. But after getting used to this, it was no problem.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not as easy as accepted. I started 4/5 months before and it took a while, and seemed very easy to get scammed. The university helped mainly students staying for a full year. It is common to send a deposit before getting a contract (also for Italian students), so I'd recommend making sure to see the apartment on a live video call before hand. I found my shared apartment on the website
Immobiliere.it
. Public transport is very slow, so I'd recommend finding somewhere close to university. The common rent was 500-700 euros for a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good chance to get to know new people, and it is kind of the only option if only staying for 6 months.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university was not helpful, but it was possible to find something in the area through websites and facebook groups.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is pretty digitalized.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are different websites you need to register on. The communication took place via university email and was pretty straightforward. Choosing courses is done online as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student mobility service and IT service were both quick to respond. Information could be found in a welcome folder given by email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The only problem were time overlaps, which meant I had to choose new courses. But besides this I had no problem joining courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help if you need it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am in the final year of my bachelor and took only courses at masters level. Academically they were okay, and not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more interaction during courses, and exercises encouraging debates and presentations. It was a good opportunity to practice oral skills, where UCPH focuses on written essays and exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "EU Institutions and Decision-making", "EU Neighbourhood Policy", "Comparative Politics", "Storia delle Istituzioni e dell'Amministrazione", "Heritage, Tourism And Sustainable Economic Development Policies"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The EU oriented courses were nice because they were in-depth and they had guest lecturers from EU institutions.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not really encounter unexpected costs. Only thing is I went out to eat and drink a lot more than at home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Basically everything is cheaper than in Denmark as I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I took part of the LUISS Run Club. Besides this I attended events from the university's Erasmus organization that organized many parties and trips. In total I went to activities like this 2/3 times per week

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attending group trips to other places, and joining sports teams to meet other people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All of Rome including less touristy areas like Prati, Pigneto, Testaccio etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. It is still Europe. The difference is mainly when and how often you go out to eat and how much you stay outside.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with Italians or be very active in searching for friends during group work etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any particularly challenges, but the tone of voice can be a bit different and people sound more angry than they are.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the culture of being outside eating, drinking and socialising all day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing early, attend the events and be open to new people, and take the opportunities the university provides.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from other European countries, that I will have contact with in the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Socialising every day in the beginning was a bit tiring.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
